Shameless creative fatigue & diversity

Meta (facebook) · 12 weeks, Jul 13 to Oct 4, 2026 · ejam-dwh.production.creative_dashboard + ai.asset_tagging_* · built 2026-10-07
The read: the account isn't short of creatives, it's running on a handful of old ones. In September spend jumped about 60% and poured into one concept (SH-16975, a third of all spend) and into ads 8+ weeks old. Fatigue is the symptom; low visual diversity is the cause. Every winner starts losing about a fifth of its ROAS by week 2, and nothing different enough is ready to take over.
56%of the last 2 weeks' spend went to creatives 8+ weeks old (mid-July: 14%)
16%went to creatives launched in the last 2 weeks (mid-July: 48%)
55 → 14creatives effectively carrying spend, Aug vs Sep
37%of the last 2 weeks' spend ($106k) is on creatives already 30%+ below their peak ROAS
−22%median ROAS drop by a creative's own week 2, versus its first two weeks

Mechanisms (named, so we can point at them)

1. The novelty half-lifeA new ad's edge is the first look. By week 2 the median creative has lost 22% of its ROAS; CTR and conversion fall together, so it's the audience tiring, not the page.
2. Paying for the second lookFrom week 5 Meta charges 17% to 31% more per thousand views to keep an old ad running: it has to dig past everyone who's already scrolled by it.
3. Entity clonesVariants that share a layout, packshot, or face read to Meta as one ad. 4 of 5 launches never reach $100 because they're competing with their own siblings.
4. One face for a different buyer87% of video spend is on talent that reads 18 to 29. Our loyalist survey says 66% of buyers are 55+. No video in 12 weeks has used 55+ talent.
5. The survivor illusionPooled, old ads look fine (wk 12+ ROAS 0.94) because only survivors keep spending. Track each ad against its own start, not against the pool.

The ad doesn't break, it wears. Click-through drops 8 to 9% and conversion about 10% in weeks 2 to 4; from week 5 the cost to be seen climbs 17 to 31%. A creative that opens at 1.3 is a 1.0 by week 3 and a 0.9 by week 7, which is exactly where the account's biggest ads are sitting now.

Through July and August new work carried 25 to 48% of spend. From the September budget jump it fell to 14 to 29% and old ads took more than half. Account ROAS rose to 0.93 on the September push, then slid to 0.78 as SH-16975-3 wore out.

August was the most diverse stretch (55 effective creatives). September is the least diverse: spend rose about 60% while the number of creatives that got a real read fell from 421 to 276, and launches reaching $100 fell to 21%. Concentration bought two good weeks (0.93) while SH-16975 still had legs, then turned into the slide to 0.78: when one ad carries a third of the account and tires, nothing different is standing behind it.

Five places we keep making the same ad: young customer-creator faces (85% of video), polished studio statics (79%), headline-over-product layouts (48%), Direct Offer as the static angle (48%, up from 24%), and evergreen everything (99%) going into Q4. Some of these lanes pay (offer promos 1.06, product grids 1.00, pop-art statics 1.04); the problem is not that they're bad, it's that Meta sees them as the same ad.

3. The creatives carrying the account right now

Top non-Cruva creatives by spend, Sep 21 to Oct 4. Code links open the asset. Status: Fatigued = 30%+ below its best 2-week ROAS; Holding = within that and ≥ 0.9; Fresh = ≤ 3 weeks old. Cruva creator clips ($32k in the same window) are left out.
▶ SH-16975-3 Fatigued
week 11 · last 2 wks $43k · contribution −$24k
ROAS peak 2.30 → now 0.64 · CPM $25 → $38 · CTR 1.75%
What worked The equal-number stat duel: 10 of our bags against 1 of theirs. The viewer does the math and closes the loop on their own, which is why it peaked at 2.30.
What held it back One young guy, one kitchen, eleven weeks, a third of all spend. Everyone the math convinces has seen it; CPM went 25 to 38 to find new eyes, and the face doesn't look like our 55+ buyer.
▶ SH-16975-2 Holding
week 10 · last 2 wks $23k · contribution −$4k
ROAS peak 1.44 → now 1.11 · CPM $28 → $38 · CTR 1.26%
What worked "How is this even legal?" over an open box. Abundance is permission: the buyer sees the whole stash before they see a price, so the offer lands as a steal.
What held it back Still above 1.0 but CPM is up 28 to 38 and CTR is flat. It's the last profitable whale and there is no successor briefed behind it.

4. How to fix it: what to make next

  1. Brief the successor at week 2, not week 8.Any creative that clears $3k at 1.0+ in its first two weeks gets three successors briefed that week. The novelty half-life says the window to replace it is weeks 2-4; today the replacement shows up after it's already at 0.8, if ever.
  2. SH-16975-3: keep the mechanic, change everything Meta can see.The 10-bags-vs-1 equal-number duel is the asset, not the kid in the kitchen. Three re-skins: a woman 55-65 on the couch at night (the survey's #1 moment, 54%), a car or office desk setting, and a static split-screen "his bag | my 10 bags" version. Same numbers, new face, new room, new format.
  3. SH-16975-2 needs a sequel before it falls under 1.0.New haul: different hands and box, Mini Bites mixed in, an older creator's voice. Abundance-as-permission is the mechanic to keep; the "How is this even legal?" line can travel.
  4. Test the buyer we actually have.Three videos with 50-65 women as talent, reason-why or daily-habit framing ("my nightly treat"), not trend-speak. Honest read: the 35-49 talent we've tried hasn't beaten 25-29, so this is a pocket test, not a proven lane, but 0% spend on the face of 66% of buyers is the single biggest diversity hole.
  5. Replace the 6-to-9-month-old statics with different-looking ones.SH-3028, SH-9428 and the SH-13376 Target pair are 27 to 39 weeks old. Keep their frames (Target permission, broccoli equivalence, $2.69 "at last"), move them out of polished studio: phone-shot lifestyle (bag on a nightstand, in a purse), pop-art, a real Target shelf photo. One Target concept, not two twins.
  6. Variants must be different scenes, not different headlines.Cap at 3 per concept, each changing at least one of: talent, setting, format (video/static/carousel), visual style. Headline-only variants are entity clones and explain most of the 4-in-5 launches that never get $100.
  7. Make the Q4 calendar now.99% evergreen going into Halloween, Thanksgiving, gifting. Seasonal was a top-3 contribution lane earlier this year. One seasonal wrapper per proven mechanic (stat duel, haul, candy drawer) gives instant visual novelty without a new idea.
  8. Track two production numbers weekly.Effective creatives carrying spend (target 30+, now 14) and share of spend on creatives ≤ 2 weeks old (target 30%+, now 16%). Both come from the same table; they'd have flagged September three weeks ago.
For the media buyer (one line): SH-16975-3 took $43k in the last two weeks at 0.64, down from a 2.30 peak, while sibling SH-16975-2 runs 1.11.
